text: Guilt can't be in two places. If Jesus bore it, you don't have to.
explanation:
In prayer one day, these words came to Joseph Prince so clearly that he got up to write them down: "Jesus cannot bear guilt while you are bearing guilt. Guilt cannot be in two places. Either it's on Him, or it's on you. If it's on you and you bear it, it cannot be on Him. Where guilt is, there can be no restoration."

It sounds simple, but it changes everything. When you've failed, carrying the guilt yourself doesn't honour God. It treats the cross as if it wasn't enough. Look to Jesus and say, "Lord, You bore this guilt. I won't carry it." Then expect Him to restore.

text: The guilt offering required restoring "its full value, add one-fifth more." Jesus became our guilt offering: 120% restoration.
explanation:
Under the law, someone who had cheated, stolen or lied about another's property had to bring an asham, a guilt offering, and "restore its full value, add one-fifth more to it." It wasn't enough to repay; the wronged party received 120%. Isaiah says the Messiah's soul was made an asham, a guilt offering. And in a psalm Jesus quoted at the Last Supper: "Then I restored that which I did not take away."

Jesus took the place of the guilty one, so He's the one who restores, and you've been made the righteous one who receives. Where the enemy has robbed you, whether of health, peace or provision, don't wallow in guilt. Say, "Because of the cross, I receive 120% restoration here."

text: "There is therefore now no condemnation": in Greek, ouden, none at all, no exceptions.
explanation:
The word Paul uses is a strong negative that shuts the door completely. Not a little condemnation, not some: none. "For those who are in Christ Jesus." Notice: not Jesus Christ, the name often used of Him in His earthly ministry, but Christ Jesus, the risen, glorified Lord at the Father's right hand. That's who you're in.

Can the glorified Christ ever be condemned? Then neither can you. He died to sin once for all: to its condemnation and judgment. You're enveloped in Him, like someone in the depths of the ocean, surrounded on every side. And verse 2 follows verse 1: "The law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus has made me free from the law of sin and death."

text: Jesus said, "Neither do I condemn you; go and sin no more." No condemnation comes first, and that's what empowers you.
explanation:
The church often gets the order backwards: "Sort out your life first, then we won't condemn you." But Jesus spoke to a woman caught in the act of adultery only hours before. First, "Neither do I condemn you." Then, "Go and sin no more."

Receiving no condemnation while you're still in your mess is what gives you the power to walk free. Psychiatrists observe that guilt lies at the root of addictions: the more guilty you feel, the more you repeat what you're ashamed of. Grace breaks the cycle. When you know how completely you're loved and forgiven, the desire for sin itself begins to fade.

text: "Look around you and be distressed. Look within you and be depressed. Look to Christ and be at rest."
explanation:
That saying is often attributed to Corrie ten Boom, and it's exactly what the accuser exploits. In Hebrew, ha-satan means the prosecutor. A prosecutor never argues the defendant's good points. He'll remind you of every failure and tell you that even your good deeds weren't good enough. The more self-occupied you become, the deeper you sink.

The way out isn't trying harder to feel better about yourself. It's looking away from yourself to Jesus and His finished work. When the enemy accuses you, tell him, "Go and check Jesus. If you find anything wrong with His obedience, come back and talk to me."

text: "I am the righteousness of God in Christ." A man in his 70s said it daily, and a 20-year addiction ended.
explanation:
A brother from South Carolina wrote that he'd smoked pot for twenty years, from his fifties into his seventies, and had tried to quit many times. After hearing testimonies, he began declaring, "I am the righteousness of God in Christ." He said it felt ridiculous, but he did it in faith. Within weeks he was free, with no withdrawal and no desire to smoke again.

That's real transformation: not gritting your teeth against something you still crave, but being freed even from the wanting. Say it in the middle of your struggle, not after you've won. It isn't a lie. It's what God says is true of you.

text: If a debtor's bill is paid but he doesn't know it, he still hides from his creditor. Believe the news.
explanation:
Imagine owing someone $10,000 you can't repay. Every time you see him, the debt weighs on your conscience. Then someone pays it for you, and more: they give him a million. He's not out of pocket because of you; he's been enriched. But if you never hear about it, or don't believe the person who tells you, you'll still avoid him and feel the weight, though the debt is gone.

That's what Hebrews means by worshippers who, "once purified, would have had no more consciousness of sins." Through the cross, God has received far more glory than our sin ever robbed Him of. Believe the messenger, and "draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith."
